Reiger Park Death Mine

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A grieving Boksburg mother has described to how she lost both her sons in a tragedy at a mine dump in Reiger Park.

Unique Selling Point:
This is a heartbreaking story about how Reiger Park parents living in fear following the tragedy. Despite countless demands to the department and the mining company to ensure the safety of the community, nothing was done. Community members believe this tragedy could have been averted.



Summary:
Chezelle Peters said that her children joined their friends for a dip at a nearby mine dump last month, without any adult supervision and without their parents' knowledge.
It's understood that when her 7-year-old son started sinking in the sand below, her 9-year-old boy sacrificed his own life to try and save him.
The devastated mother is now seeking justice, insisting that the tragedy could have been prevented if the area had been secured.
Chezelle says she just wants an apology from authorities who were negligent enough to leave the site unsecured.
Reiger Park parents are now living in renewed fear following this tragedy, like grandmother, Lydia Kruger, who said that her young grandchildren had also been swimming at the mine.
"The children are swimming. Every day I have to stand by the stairs and shout at my grandsons. I even went there many times to beat them up inside," Grandma Lydia said.
The community has raised the safety and security issue with authorities, the mine and the Mineral Resources Department for years now asking for a fence to be erected, however, no one seems to be taking the request seriously.

Further information:
Objective of the story:
1. Confront DRDGOLD Limited- the mining company that owns the mine dump- about why they have not installed a securing fence or wall when the mine is close to a community with young children.
2. Confront the department Mineral Resource and find out if the department has instructed DRDGOLD to secure the dangerous areas around their mines in Reiger Park.

Press Release:



Reiger Park Mine Deaths - Busisiwe / Mac

In the old suburb of Reiger Park on Johannesburg’s East Rand the poor post-closure management of massive gold mines is costing lives. Old and abandoned mines is one thing (and there are over 6000 of them in the country) – but here we look at the tragedy of one family losing two young sons in an accident that should not have been possible. The seven and nine year old boys disappeared into the quicksand in the area he community calls “The Dooms” in an old mine whose owners are known. DRD Gold is still in business and it has neither fenced off their property nor has guards posted to protect the community. Formerly designated “coloured” under Apartheid’s Group Areas Act, people were settled right next to the mine, on land that shouldn’t be for residential purposes. The community has campaigned for decades for safeguards to be put in place – it’s after all the same site where the older men who are now fathers used to play as children. The problem is that old. The Department of Mineral Resources and Energy has taken no steps to fix the problem and the mine told us it is considering establishing a monitoring forum with the community.

Script:


VO - No parent should ever outlive their child.

But on this tragic day, Chezelle Peters, had to bury not one, but two
of her sons - 9-year old Na- sri and 7-year old Wyatt.

SOUND UP - Chezelle Peters
00:32They got missing on the 19th. I knew something was wrong. In my brain, I
decided they were abducted or dead.
VO - Her gut feeling wasn’t wrong...
As a resident of Reiger Park, on Johannesburg's East Rand ,Chezelle
always warned her sons not to go anywhere near the mine dump,
just a stone’s throw away from their home.
SOUND UP - CHEZELLE PETERS
00:59 I would always say to them, don’t go to the mine that place will swallow you.
VO – For the boys, the temptation of fun in the water trumped her
warnings, and it cost them dearly.
On the 19th of January, Chezelle went looking for her boys when they
hadn't returned home by late afternoon. She learned that they'd been
seen by other kids, swimming AT the mine dump. In a panic, she called
the police and asked community members to help her search for her
boys.
Their clothes were only discovered the next day next to a puddle of
rainwater. Chezelle believes her boys were unaware that the water would
turn the sand into a deadly sludge.
CHEZELLE PETERS – GRIEVING MOTHER - MVI_1114
01:44 I actually broke down because it’s a very cruel way to die. It’s not good.
Especially since they’re my boys. And I was just thinking, did they call out for their
mom?
01:58 Even as a child, the first thing they call out is mom. When you’re hurt, when you
have problems, you think about your mother. That’s like your comfort zone.
VO - It also took rescue personnel two days to recover their bodies.
SOUND UP - CHEZELLE
22:01:51:47 I was calling ”Nasri, Wyatt”. As I was doing that I would get all teary
calling out for them.
VO – Quicksand is a solution of sand and water that, when disturbed,
creates a kind of liquified soil that can literally swallow a trapped body.
22:06:13:22 I wanted to see that they drowned and that they were there. When the
water was drained and I couldn’t see them, my heart actually sank because I knew the
mine swallowed them. I didn't want to see them digging them out. So I decided to go. I
actually broke down.
CHEZELLE PETERS – GRIEVING MOTHER - MVI_1114
MAC - What would you do most when you were together?
CHEZELLE - 57:47:22 Nasri was like a DIY, he was always busy building
something. If there is sticky tape in the house, he will find stuff that needs to be
taped somewhere. If I buy new nails he’d find something to do with them.
58:08:23 - Wyatt would go around irritating everybody. He was a joker.
VO - While Chezelle is left to confront her trauma, the death of her boys
has raised questions about the safety of other children in Reiger Park.
LINK – MVI_0006 - Situated opposite the Reiger Park flats is the mining dump
where Chezelle's two boys drowned and community members tell me that
many of the kids who live here often cross over to the other side for a dip in the
water without any adult supervision.
VO – It is the responsibility of the Department of Mineral Resources to
evaluate environmental impact projections submitted by mining
companies.
David van Wyk is from corporate monitoring organisation, the
Benchmark Foundation. He says living close to mine dumps exposes
people to various physical and health-related risks.
DAVID VAN WYK – BENCHMARK FOUNDATION
23:38:49:16 - ... the dust that is in this mine dump contains arsenic, uranium,
cylica, copper, iron, lead and so on. And all those heavy metals pose a danger
to the communities around them. 23:39:40:15 - ... there would be problems
with skin and cancer. 23:36:57:46 - ... in this community you find a lot of
problems with respiratory diseases. 23:37:13:10 - You find a lot of skin
problems. Things like eczema and so on...
VO - Van Wyk has extensively researched the impact of mines near
residential spaces, and says no one should have to call this place home.

DAVID VAN WYK – BENCHMARK FOUNDATION
23:39:05:44 - Under apartheid these communities like this one here was
located here to remove people from what we called white areas. 23:39:23:45 -
This was the least valuable land that is why the land was available for coloured
and black communities.

VO – Chezelle is as much in shock today as she was on the day her
children were pulled out of the quicksand.

BREATHER/PAUSE IN SOUND
LINK – MCI_1218 - No entry signs around the mine are easy to spot but the
same cannot be said about a fence and security personnel. And these are
issues that the community previously raised with authorities however nothing
has been done.
VO - For decades, residents have been demanding that the mine secures
the area with a sturdy fence.
RESIDENT - MVI_0019

00:54 we have little dams forming especially with the terrestrial rains we have. And we
now have rain water, whenever there is an overflow of water, running down the streets
of Reiger park and it goes right into the Cinderella dam. this area is toxic,
VO – The poor state of security at the site has long been a problem.

RESIDENT - MVI_0021

00:19:17:35 I moved in 2016 and ever since it was always a problem this side,
because you have to look after other peoples children that will go on the other side of
the fence to go and play
VO - Parents here are in constant fear for their children’s lives. There are
15 mining companies responsible for 26 mine dumps close to this
community.

VO: In July 2020, a 5-year old boy drowned near a mineshaft in this area.
Three years earlier at another mineshaft, rescuers abandoned efforts to
retrieve the body of a young child who had fallen into a deep cavity filled
with acidic water.

Chezelle says her journey to recovery has been especially rocky since
the place where her boys lost their lives is a just short walk from their
home.
Gareth Phillips is the father of the boys. This is the first time he has come
to this spot since the boys died.
GARETH PHILLIPS – GRIEVING FATHER
MAC - 23:59:06:48 You grew up in Reiger park, do you have memories of this
place, was it always open like this?
GARETH - 23:59:11:01 – Yah, it’s been like this all my life. We used to have
access to this all the time. 23:59:26:12 – ... I went through a similar situation
where I almost drowned. 23:59:34:26 - My uncle was the one who who helped me.
VO – But there was no one to save his boys.
GARETH PHILLIPS – GRIEVING FATHER
00:01:30:30 - ... I actually got emotional when we got to the spot again, it was
starting to roll again. It’s tough.
ffVO - Confusing is the word. Despite Nasri and Wyatt’s tragic deaths, the
community here says nothing’s been done to improve security.
VO – The Department of Mineral Resources and Energy initially agreed to
discuss the life-threatening issues impacting the people of Reiger Park.
But, at the last minute, chose to send an email instead.
The two-liner notes our enquiry and says it regrets the sad loss of life.
The department, it adds, plans to “investigate the matter to ascertain the
facts and act accordingly.”
DAVID VAN WYK – BENCHMARK FOUNDATION
MAC – 23:41:13:05 - Surely if government knows that this is a problem that
these mines cause, they should be a lot stricter and controlled.
DAVID - 23:41:23:06 – We have got a government of mine bosses
unfortunately and we have very senior members of the ruling party who sit on
the boards of these mining companies and they are shareholders as well.
MAC – 23:42:45:25 - So it’s a matter or profits over people, right?
DAVID – 23:42:48:05 - It’s a matter of profits over people, and the departments
problem is that they see their role as being that of promoting mining instead of regulating mine.
VO – DRD Gold, THE MINE COMPANY IN QUESTION, had a bit more to
say but also shied away from an interview. IN A WRITTEN RESPONSE,
the mine SAID it had been in touch with the family.
GARETH PHILLIPS – GRIEVING FATHER
00:00:42:48 - ... they might have spoken to the counsellor or members of the
community but they haven’t come to us.
VO – Though the company provided money for the funeral, it has yet to
reach out directly to the family.
DRD Gold explains that often, fences “are either stolen or vandalized,adding that guards posted on the site in the past were invariably
attacked, robbed and assaulted.”
The company is considering collaborating with residents to “establish a
monitoring forum”. The mine promises that the site in question “will be
sustainably repurposed with the risks associate with an active mining
site being eliminated.”
All of this comes as no comfort to heartbroken parents whose lives will
never be the same.
GARETH PHILLIPS – GRIEVING FATHER
00:01:03:15 - They are letting us down, that’s the feeling I’m getting.
00:00:09:24 - It’s hard, I don’t even have words to explain because it’s so
overwhelming and confusing.
CHEZELLE PETERS – GRIEVING MOTHER - MVI_1114
I break down in the mornings when I wake up. And at night. There is an
emptiness that is left behind. I don’t think it’s going to go away. It’s hurt and
emptiness that one will have to live with.

"The children are swimming. Every day I have to stand by the stairs and shout at my grandsons. I even went there many times to beat them up inside," Grandma Lydia said. The community has raised the safety and security issue with authorities, the mine and the Mineral Resources Department for years now asking for a fence to be erected, however, no one seems to be taking the request seriously.

Confront the department Mineral Resource and find out if the department has instructed DRDGOLD to secure the dangerous areas around their mines in Reiger Park.
